articleTitle: Numerical study of the coupling of transient fields of ESD into a cavity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The problem of shielding sensitive measurement equipment, computers and control devices, against the influence of disturbing electromagnetic fields is by no means new. Usually, the metallic shields are used to protect equipment, the sensitive electronic parts of which can be disturbed or even destroyed by transient EM fields. Practical shielding enclosures always contain many apertures such as vents, cable feed-through and seams, which allow electromagnetic energy to couple into the structure. This paper presents a numerical study of the coupling of transient fields radiated during electrostatic discharge (ESD) into the metallic enclosure with an aperture. Computer simulation of the ESD is done using an electrodynamic method based on the method of moments (MoM) in the time domain for discharging bodies of revolution, located near the grounded plane. For a discharging structure like a spheroid the calculated currents and fields are compared with experimental data and are shown to be accurate for EMC applications. Such realistic fields are used in this paper as incident fields to investigate aperture penetration into cavities. The time domain analysis is done using the FDTD method.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of ESD from cone
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The paper is devoted to a computer simulation of the electrostatic discharge (ESD) from cone. The numerical model is based on the electrodynamical consideration of the problem. The method of moments (MoM) in the time domain, coupled with a nonlinear model of the arc, is used to develop an efficient algorithm of the ESD simulation. The transient currents and fields are analysed from an EMC point of view. The results of numerical simulation are shown to be in a good agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: Investigation and optimization of a sensor for partial discharge detection on high voltage XLPE cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: Based on the experimental investigations a simple theoretical model for the simulation of partial discharge (PD) detection on high voltage XLPE-insulated cables has been developed. The model handles radial symmetric sensors. The dependence of sensitivity on geometrical characteristics of the sensor is investigated experimentally and theoretically. Results of computer simulation are in a good agreement with experimental data derived for such sensors.

articleTitle: Closed solutions of a nonlinear integral equation arisen in the antenna arrays synthesis theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The nonlinear integral equation describing solutions of the synthesis problem of an equidistant linear antenna array is investigated. The equation is obtained and solved numerically. The new solution has an analytical form with a small numbers of complex parameters calculated from a set of transcendental equations. The numerical results are presented. The results can be generalized for other problems described by the discrete Fourier transformation.

articleTitle: New materials design: scattering problems and the method of auxiliary sources
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The development of the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) to 2-D and 3-D scattering problems upon the objects of complicated shape and of complex materials is considered. Application of MAS to the problems of anisotropy, chirality and biisotropy is shown. The algorithm used to determine the solution in a general case is described, and the new numerical and physical results of investigating specific objects in a wide frequency range are presented. A program complex for studying the radiation, propagation, scattering and absorption processes in complex media is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Diffraction by impedance wedge with curved faces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The problem of plane wave diffraction by an imperfectly conducting wedge BOA with curved convex faces OA and OB is treated and the short-wave asymptotic of the scattered field applicable in the vicinities of faces and near the tangents OA' and OB' to the faces is found. We show that the creeping waves are excited in these domains. In the main term of the asymptotics these waves coincides with the waves excited by a source at a smooth convex surface multiplied by a constant factor which is found in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic wave reflection by multi-layer periodic structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A method is suggested for analysis of electromagnetic wave reflection by a periodic structure that has a finite number of elements. It is based on the use of the semi-infinite structure reflection operator.

articleTitle: The method of auxiliary sources for microwave and ultrasonic imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A holographic technique based on the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) for microwave and ultrasonic imaging is presented. The essence of the method is the visualization of the scattered field singularities (SFS). The idea is that any discontinuity of the electromagnetic characteristics of the investigated media causes remission of the incident field and represents the SFS of the scattered field. The proposed imaging method is sensitive to such singularities and gives the possibility to visualize and detect the insertions in the area under investigation.

articleTitle: Calculation of waves scattered in irregular waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: Wave scattering problems in irregular waveguides are investigated. The proposed algorithm for solving such problems is based on the reduction of the scattering problem to an interior boundary value problem in the irregular section. This problem is solved in general form by the boundary integral equation method and then the solutions in regular and irregular sections are matched. The scalar Dirichlet problem with excitation by a wave, incident from infinity, is considered. The approach is applied to a test problem and numerical results are compared with the ones obtained by the cross section method.

articleTitle: Modification of successive approximation method in generalized spectrum problems for quadratic matrix beams
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The case of the eigenvalue problem of the quadratic matrix beam is proposed. The method permits one to calculate all eigenpairs of the matrix beam. With this aim, the generalized eigenvalue problem is reduced to a linear problem. Then, the modified successive approximations method is used for calculation of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. This permits the use of the information obtained from the iterations, to obtain the first eigenpair and all the following ones more quickly. Some numerical examples are considered.

articleTitle: Improved evaluation of the resonance spectral parameters of sound scattering from the spherical thin elastic shell
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The resonance characteristics of the complex amplitudes of acoustic pressure scattering by an elastic thin spherical shell are investigated. In the R-matrix approach the analytical relations for the approximate determination of the partial resonance frequencies and widths are found. The conditions for effective "background" scattering suppression and selection of resonances caused by sound radiation of the shell on the bending and membrane vibrations are obtained. For quadrupolar sound scattering by shells of average thickness a correlation between the widths of the spectral lines of the zero order symmetrical Lamb wave (membrane type of vibration) and the chemical type of the shell metal is discovered.

articleTitle: The method of auxiliary sources for investigation of pulse scattering in time domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The extension of the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) into time domain is presented. The MAS has been extensively applied to the wide class of steady electromagnetic processes problems as one of the efficient tools. It provides the faster algorithm for simulation and visualization of electromagnetic periodical and transient processes in real scale of time. Particular efficiency occurs for closed scatterers. With the help of MAS in the time domain it is easy to follow the formation of eigenfields of various structures. The transient scattering on a cylinder with a longitudinal slot is considered as an example.

articleTitle: Accumulating, directing and focusing properties of 2-D and 3-D objects of biisotropic materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A biisotropic medium is an optically active medium that may be applied to develop devices with new physical properties. In this paper, resulting from the solution of a complicated boundary problem, the high frequency properties of 2-D and 3-D biisotropic objects are investigated, and the physical properties of these objects are revealed and analyzed.

articleTitle: Scattering of SH-waves by a crack-like inclusion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A thin-walled flat elastic inclusion of low rigidity is perfectly bonded to a surrounding elastic matrix and subjected to an incident plane harmonic SH-wave. The displacement fields in the wave zone of a scatterer are evaluated to the null order by the methods of matched asymptotic expansions and boundary integral equation, with the thickness-to-diameter ratio as the perturbation parameter.

articleTitle: Diffraction of EM waves by perforated screen with finite width
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A finite width screen with perfect conductivity and double periodicity slots was considered. Let such the system be placed in an isotropic medium and be excited at an arbitrary angle by a plane electromagnetic (EM) wave. We solved the problem of finding the field distribution in space and calculated its electromagnetic parameters. The problem was solved by means of the method of subsections. Resulting from the calculation, the dependence of the field transmission coefficient on the different parameters and the field distribution inside the waveguide were obtained. An analysis of the structure was also conducted.

articleTitle: On the problem of nonlinear interaction of uniformly exited finite-amplitude sound beams
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: On the basis of the parabolic (quasi-optic) approximation the nonlinear interaction of finite uniformly exited sound beams is investigated. The method of presentation of primary excitation as a superposition of Gaussian beams is used. The effect of the near-field oscillation of amplitude and phase of the primary beams is accounted for. The amplitudes of the difference frequency and second harmonic components in the acoustic beam are analyzed numerically.

articleTitle: The algorithm of modeling of radio channel in cellular communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The authors present an algorithm for modeling wave propagation in the case of high density of buildings. It allows the optimal placement of base station antennas in cellular communication systems. The algorithm is ready to use for computing the total electromagnetic field including waves reflected by buildings.

articleTitle: Approximate expressions of the Ishimaru parabolic equation analysis within the problem of EM impulse propagation through diffusing dissipative media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: We show that the approach utilized in Ishimarus's (1977) model to describe a time EM impulse shape behavior in homogeneous nondissipative scattering medium can be extended to inhomogeneous dissipative media. The model extension is based on Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dissipative stochastic process application. We also derive the explicit expression for the problem Green function. The time-dependent term of the Green function is of a Laguerre type for all the considered conditions. In the case of Laguerre-like input pulses it allowed us to show the Laguerre properties of the output pulses.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of resonance diffraction characteristics of cascaded gratings (TM-case)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The problem of a plane wave scattering on a multielement diffraction grating is considered. The diffracted field is sought for as a single-layer potential. The technique of integration path deformation is utilized for Green function's calculation. An accounting of a singularity of the integrand on a specially chosen part of the integration path is adopted to derive a numerical solution. To reduce the computation time for Sommerfeld-type integral calculations essentially a Lagrange-type interpolation polynomial of several variables is used. By an integration path deformation and accounting for residues from poles the estimation of the Green's function at infinity is provided. A two-layered cascaded grating with two curvilinear screens on the period was considered.

articleTitle: About the determination of the shape of a body, situated nearby other bodies, from its several scattering patterns
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The method described, gives the possibility to make some conclusions about the shape and situation of a body from any of its scattering patterns by different illuminations. It is not necessary to know the illumination field. The method was earlier described and illustrated for a scatter in free space. The main idea of the method is expound and it is generalized for the case, when other bodies are situated in the field.

articleTitle: Closed resonator of special form with metallic and impedance walls and waveguide excitation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The problem of the waveguide excitation of the closed resonator of lengthened form with variable height, impedance upper wall and metallic lower and side ones, is considered. An iterative procedure joining the cross section method and method of partial domains, is proposed.

articleTitle: Some new vanishing solutions of linear antenna synthesis problem according to prescribed amplitude radiation pattern
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The synthesis problem of a linear antenna according to the given amplitude radiation pattern in the variational statement is considered. As a criterion of optimization the least-square deviation between the prescribed and obtained amplitude patterns is taken. The analytical vanishing solutions of Euler's equation are obtained. These solutions are presented as functions with complex parameters which are calculated easily from the set of transcendental equations. These solutions are better for such prescribed patterns which are vanishing too. Some numerical results are shown.

articleTitle: A method of generalized separation of variables for solving two-dimensional integral equations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The concept of separation of variables traditionally unites with the Fourier method of solving of differential equations in partial derivatives. The most universal scheme of its many generalizations is described by Kaleniuk et al. (1993). Its main idea consists of a choice of a problem partial solution with a more complicated structure. In the solution of many-dimensional integral equations a different variational-iterative generalization of variables separation is used. The solution is obtained approximately in the form of a series. The members of this series are functions with separated variables. They are calculating successively to satisfy the condition of minimization of corresponding functionals. Each new step of the method permits one to calculate a new member of the series and also makes the solution of the equation accurate. In this paper the method of the generalized separation of variables for solving a two-dimensional integral equation is set forth, its particle basis is examined, and some numerical results are shown.

articleTitle: Wave penetration through and reflection from the combined multilayered many-element gratings with dielectric layer and metal screen
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A rigorous theory of the combined multilayered many-element cylindrical gratings is presented. The boundary problems are transformed to solving algebraic sets of equations for the multipole coefficients of the spectrum of scattered field. The numerical results for the electrodynamic characteristics of the combined gratings are obtained and analyzed. The combined gratings of various profile and filling with dielectric layers and metal screens are widely used in antenna and microwave engineering as elements of reflecting and matching devices, antenna radomes, microwave resonators and filters, wave transformers etc. To control the transmission, reflection and polarization characteristics of the gratings, it is necessary to provide the capability to change the interior structure of the grating spacing. In this paper, the combined multilayered many-element cylindrical gratings are suggested and investigated to provide this capability. A rigorous theory of combined multilayered many-element circular cylindrical gratings is proposed, and some numerical results are obtained and discussed.

articleTitle: High resolution image restoration based on inverse problem solution using iterative methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: In this paper the implementation of iterative methods to image restoration is presented. To describe the image formation process an observation model is given. Comparative analysis of different iterative image restoration methods is performed. Quantitative confirmation of image quality improvement is carried out in l/sub 2/-norm error.

articleTitle: Scalar wave diffraction by axially symmetrical system of infinitely thin perfectly conducting circular rings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: A new strong mathematically rigorous and numerically efficient method for solving the boundary value problem of scalar wave diffraction by a system of infinitely thin circular ring shaped screens is proposed. The method is based on the combination of the orthogonal polynomials approach and on the ideas of the methods of analytical regularisation. The solution is generalisation of the investigation done for one ring. As a result of the suggested regularisation procedure, the initial boundary value problem was equivalently reduced to the infinite system of the linear algebraic equations of the second kind, i.e. to an equation of the type (I+H)x=b, x, b/spl isin/l/sub 2/ in the space l/sub 2/ of square summable sequences. This equation can be solved numerically by means of a truncation method with, in principle, any required accuracy.

articleTitle: Wave scattering by wedge with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The scattering problems for surfaces with different boundary conditions on their parts are of interest to many investigators. This is connected with the possibility of factorizing the vector Wiener-Hopf equations derived by Fourier integral transform application. The possibility of extension of such problems due to use of Kontorvich-Lebedev integral transform is shown.

articleTitle: Polarizing filters, converters and modulators based on controllable microstrip diffraction arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The microstrip diffraction arrays applications in the microwave area are considered as the problems of polarizing filters, depolarizers and polarizing modulators design. The mathematical simulation as a method of the investigation is selected because of the high cost and the complexity of arrays experimental research.

articleTitle: The analytic-numerical solution method of the nonlinear problems of the antennas phase synthesis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The phase synthesis problems of antennas according to the prescribed amplitude radiation pattern in the variational statement are considered. Optimization of the considered functionals reduces the problems to the nonlinear Euler's equation set concerning the phase radiation pattern and unknown phase distribution of a current. The appropriate linear equation for determination of the branch points is obtained. For investigation of this equation the numerical approach is used.

articleTitle: Use of the thin coatings to control characteristics of radiating and scattering objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of III International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory. (IEEE Cat. No.98EX163)
abstract: The possibility of controlling the radiation and scattering characteristics of an object without changing its geometry, but only changing the shape, thickness and electrodynamic properties of the coating is considered. The numerical algorithm used to solve the boundary problem is described, and some numerical results for 2-D and 3-D objects with different types of coatings are presented and analyzed.
